user.title: Connect to the AutoLedger add-on
user.description: Install and start the AutoLedger add-on first. The token is on the add-on's Settings page.

data_description.url: Usually http://<something>-autoledger:8099. The suggestion is taken from your installed add-ons.

hassio_confirm.title: AutoLedger add-on found
hassio_confirm.description: Connect Home Assistant to the AutoLedger add-on? Afterwards, add your cars and home charger on the integration page.

reauth_confirm.title: New API token needed
reauth_confirm.description: The add-on refused the token, for example because a new one was created. Copy the token from the add-on's Settings page.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the AutoLedger add-on at this URL.

user.title: Which car?
user.description: Pick the vehicle from the AutoLedger add-on and its odometer sensor. The next step suggests the other entities of the same device.

entities.title: Entities of {vehicle}
entities.description: Everything except the odometer is optional, but each entity adds detections: fuel level for refuels, battery level for public charging, location for places.

data.latitude: Latitude (if there is no device tracker)
data.longitude: Longitude (if there is no device tracker)
data.days_to_service: Days to service (the car's own countdown)
data.distance_to_service: Distance to service (the car's own countdown)

data_description.car_timestamp: Cloud-connected cars report with a delay. With this, records get the car's own time.
data_description.fuel_unit: Litres, or % of the tank (the tank size from the add-on is used to convert).
data_description.days_to_service: Shown next to your maintenance schedules in AutoLedger as a cross-check.
data_description.fuel_price: Used as the suggested price of a detected refuel. Without it, the price of your last refuel is suggested.

data.min_trip_km: Trip when the car moved at least
data.refuel_min_l: Refuel when the tank rises at least
data.external_charge_min_pct: Public charge when the battery rises at least
data.idle_min_pct: Climate & standby when the parked battery drops at least
data.idle_min_l: Climate & standby when the parked tank drops at least

boost.name: Snapshot boost (fresh car data on local hints)
boost.description: Cloud cars upload when they park, but Home Assistant only sees it at the integration's next poll. With a refresh service, the Collector asks for fresh data when the home charger starts or stops, and when one of the people below leaves or arrives home. That gives trips the right start and end.

data.boost_persons: People whose leaving or arriving home hints a drive
data.boost_max_per_day: At most this many refreshes per day

data_description.boost_service: Action of the car's integration that fetches fresh data, for example lynkco.force_update_data. Leave empty to switch boost off.

data.latitude: Latitude (if there is no device tracker)
data.longitude: Longitude (if there is no device tracker)
data.days_to_service: Days to service (the car's own countdown)
data.distance_to_service: Distance to service (the car's own countdown)

data.min_trip_km: Trip when the car moved at least

data.external_charge_min_pct: Public charge when the battery rises at least
data.idle_min_pct: Climate & standby when the parked battery drops at least
data.idle_min_l: Climate & standby when the parked tank drops at least

abort.entry_not_loaded: The AutoLedger integration is not running. Check the connection to the add-on first.
abort.no_vehicles: All vehicles of the add-on are already linked. Add a vehicle in the AutoLedger panel first.

error.unknown_service: This action does not exist in Home Assistant. Use the domain.action form, for example lynkco.force_update_data.

user.title: Home charger
user.description: Charge sessions are measured with the charger's total energy counter and priced per kWh with your electricity price.

data.name: Name
data.fixed_price: Fixed price per kWh (if there is no price sensor)

data_description.power: Optional. Only used to notice the end of a session sooner; energy always comes from the counter.
data_description.price: For example your dynamic tariff. When it is unavailable, the fixed price or the add-on's fallback price is used.

data.name: Name
data.fixed_price: Fixed price per kWh (if there is no price sensor)

abort.entry_not_loaded: The AutoLedger integration is not running. Check the connection to the add-on first.

addon_unreachable.title: AutoLedger add-on unreachable
addon_unreachable.description: {count} records are waiting because the add-on cannot be reached ({error}). They are kept and delivered as soon as it is running again. Check that the add-on is started.

not_loaded.message: The AutoLedger Collector is not set up.

not_collected.message: This vehicle has no Collector vehicle entry. Add it under the AutoLedger integration first.

add_refuel.name: Add refuel
add_refuel.description: Adds a refuel to AutoLedger. Give two of litres, total and price per litre.

odometer.name: Odometer
odometer.description: Odometer at the time of the refuel, for L/100 km.

station.name: Station
station.description: Name or place of the station.

add_charge.name: Add charge
add_charge.description: Adds a charge away from home to AutoLedger.

total.name: Total
total.description: Amount paid. Leave empty to use the price per kWh.

timestamp.name: Time
timestamp.description: When the charge started. Default: now.

add_odometer.name: Add odometer reading
add_odometer.description: Adds an odometer reading to AutoLedger.

timestamp.name: Time
timestamp.description: When it was read. Default: now.

resync.name: Resync
resync.description: Sends waiting records to the add-on now and refreshes the sensors.

backfill.name: Backfill
backfill.description: Reads the recorded history of the vehicle's entities from the start date up to when live tracking began, and adds the trips, refuels, public charges and odometer readings found. Running it twice adds nothing twice. Home charge sessions are not backfilled.

start.name: Start date
start.description: Home Assistant keeps about 10 days of history by default.
